24.text: The other variety of bow (Fig. 69) was made of a single piece of wood,

25.text: mostly larch, but occasionally birch or pine, found among the driftwood on

26.text: the coast. It was strengthened by a wrapping of birch-bark or sinew, and in

27.text: addition had a plaited-sinew backing. Occasionally even a “double-wooded”

28.text: bow would have a sinew backing, not only among the Chukchee, but also

29.text: among the Yukaghir and the Lamut.

30.text: The lashing (Fig. 70, a) was of the western type, so called by John

31.text: Murdoch, with a single sinew cable secured about the body of the bow in

32.text: half-hitches, with extra strengthening on both bends. This type of lashing

33.text: has been described by John Murdoch as characteristic of the bow of north-

34.text: eastern Siberia, with the occasional mixture of the so-called Arctic type.¹ Small

35.text: ivory levers (Fig. 71, a) were used in twisting up the cords of sinew on the

36.text: back of the bow, making them into a cable. In shape they are identical
